items.title: How gamification can nudge employees to act more sustainably
items.summary: AstraZeneca and Amgen are among the winners of a competition that demonstrates how gamification can motivate companies and employees to tackle sustainability challenges.

items.title: 9 novels for the sustainability-minded reader
items.summary: Vacation itineraries and long flights have a way of making room for fiction.

items.title: Why data center companies Equinix and Oracle are buying fuel cells
items.summary: The “speed to power” ambitions of big cloud computing service providers and data center companies are boosting installations of on-site fuel cells, particularly those made by Bloom Energy.

items.title: Sustainability loans for palm oil firms linked to deforestation, report warns
items.summary: Banks have been accused of funding palm oil companies linked to deforestation and human rights violations via loans tied to corporate sustainability targets and performance.

items.title: Government’s procurement reforms prioritise jobs over net-zero
items.summary: The Government has announced a new weighting system for prospective public contracts that assesses whether spending supports UK jobs and communities, while criteria like net-zero requirements have been cut.

items.title: Heineken UK launches regenerative barley programme
items.summary: Heineken UK has launched a regenerative malting barley programme that will pay UK farmers a premium on regenerative barley yields as part of efforts to expand the use of regenerative agriculture across its brewing supply chain.

items.title: Heatwaves and drought cost UK farmers £390m, research suggests
items.summary: This year's exceptionally hot and dry conditions may have cut UK harvests by almost £400m according to provisional estimates.

items.title: Factcheck: How nuclear, gas, wind and solar power are affected during heatwaves
items.summary: Heatwaves are becoming more likely and more intense due to climate change, impacting sources of power generation around the world as they work to meet increased demand.
